Seatward
SEET-ward
adv. (toward the seat; in the phrase to the mercy seatward, facing the mercy seat)
A compound of seat and the directional suffix -ward, Old English -weard, meaning turned toward, as in homeward and heavenward. The Hebrew is simply el, toward.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The making of the ark is described twice, and the second account closes with the direction of the cherubim's faces: “And the cherubims spread out their wings on high, and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another; even to the mercy seatward were the faces of the cherubims” (Exodus 37:9). Seatward means toward the seat, and the detail is doctrine. The cherubim do not face outward as guards, nor upward as worshippers of the air; they face down and in, toward the blood-sprinkled lid of the ark. What they look at is the place where atonement is made. God had told Moses where He would meet with Israel: “And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony” (Exodus 25:22). Beneath the lid lay the broken law; above it the blood; between the cherubim the glory. The writer to the Hebrews gathers it in a phrase: “And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat” (Hebrews 9:5). Peter says the angels desire to look into these things. The gaze of heaven is turned toward the propitiation.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): -WARD, a termination denoting direction, as in homeward, heavenward; SEATWARD, toward the seat.

WARD, a termination signifying direction or tendency to, as in homeward, heavenward.

SEAT, n. That on which one sits; the place of sitting.

MERCY-SEAT, the propitiatory; the lid or covering of the ark of the covenant.

Exodus 37:9 says the faces of the cherubims were to the mercy seatward.

Hebrew el, toward.

Key Scripture

Exo 37:9 — "And the cherubims spread out their wings on high, and covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another; even to the mercy seatward were the faces of the cherubims."

Exo 25:22 — "And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel."

Heb 9:5 — "And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly."

Modern Corruption

Propitiation is removed from the centre of the atonement, so that the mercy seat becomes a symbol of divine kindness in general and the blood that was sprinkled on it is treated as primitive.

expand to see more

A long line of liberal and now progressive-evangelical writers reject penal substitution, calling the sprinkled blood of the mercy seat a vestige of primitive religion and offering instead a moral-influence or Christ-the-Victor account standing alone. The objection is not new, and it always requires the same move: the hilasterion, the propitiatory, must be reinterpreted as mere expiation or as a picture of God's solidarity with sufferers.

Exodus 37:9 answers with the direction of two golden faces. The cherubim look at the place of blood. Paul says Christ was set forth a propitiation through faith in His blood, using the very word the Greek Old Testament uses for the mercy seat, and declares the purpose: that God might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth. Substitutionary penal atonement is not an awkward strand within the doctrine; it is the thing the cherubim were made to stare at.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Seat plus the directional -ward; Exodus 37:9 turns the cherubim's faces to the mercy seatward.

expand to see more

Old English -weard, turned toward, as in homeward and heavenward.

Hebrew el, toward.

Exodus 37:9 is the only occurrence of seatward in the Authorized Version.

The cherubim face down and in, toward the place of atonement.

Hebrews 9:5 calls them the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat.
